Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no explicit clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Picks disease group reported—the sample comprises PNFA, SD, and a nonaphasic SOC/EXEC subgroup but bvFTD is not explicitly identified and MRI analyses focus on PNFA/SD), I6 (no between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls reported), I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level result from a bvFTD target sample; model fit is reported over region-of-interest only). NeuroStore extraction shows only within-group regression and ROI-based VBM results (Talairach) for PNFA/SD; no qualifying whole-brain bvFTD vs control coordinates or contrasts are provided. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study uses FDG-PET and reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with MNI coordinates, and adequate sample sizes; however the sample is described only as 'FTD' without explicit identification of behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease. Therefore I4 (must include clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick's disease) is not satisfied. Because the between-group contrast compares a pooled FTD patient group to controls, it does not clearly present a bvFTD-only vs. control contrast, so I6 (between-group contrast specifically comparing bvFTD group to controls, unpooled) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET), I5 (sufficient N in patient and control groups), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise result), I8 (coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6. Full text is complete as provided.

The study meets several inclusion criteria: it used VBM (I3), included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=58) (I4), has sufficient patient and control group sizes (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results consistent with whole-brain evidence (I7) with acceptable reporting (I8). However, it does not report any between-group contrast that directly compares the bvFTD group to controls (the reported analyses are cross-subject VBM regressions across a mixed sample relating empathic measures). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. Imaging modality is VBM (gray matter volume structural morphometry) (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD n=19) and healthy controls (n=20) (I4, I5). The NeuroStore extraction shows whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (model fit over: whole brain; thresholding FWE; coordinates in MNI; peaks reported in a table), providing between-group/ cross-subject regression results and coordinate tables (I6, I7, I8). Analyses report peaks for semantic and emotional congruity and control regressors across the cohort, and syndromic group is included as a model term; whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Given the reported VBM whole-brain coordinates and explicit patient group (bvFTD) comparisons to controls, the study should be included in the review.

The study is excluded because it does not report any between-group contrasts comparing the bvFTD group to controls in stereotactic space (fails inclusion criterion I6). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM/structural morphometry), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample using consensus criteria), I5 (patient group size >=6; control group reported in abstract and patients n>6), I7 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-patient analyses). No exclusion criteria from the list apply (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). Therefore the paper is ineligible for the meta-analysis that requires between-group bvFTD vs control contrasts. Full text was sufficiently represented in the provided document.

This study reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM (gray-matter density) contrasts in MNI space comparing patient groups to controls. It includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia cases, including fvFTD (bvFTD) and pathologically confirmed Pick disease (PiD). At least one qualifying between-group contrast meets sample-size requirements: the PiD analysis reports a patient subgroup totaling 7 (fvFTD 5, SD 1, PNFA 1) within a total N=27, implying >=6 patients and >=6 controls, and reports whole-brain coordinate peaks (Table 2). Imaging modality, whole-brain voxelwise inference, and coordinate reporting satisfy I3, I7, and I8. The sample includes bvFTD/ fvFTD and Pick disease (I4), and the PiD contrast meets the group-size threshold (I5) and is a between-group contrast in MNI (I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not disallowed modality).

The study reports task-based fMRI (Exp 1) and whole-brain morphometric VBM results (Analysis 1) and includes a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD patients to demographically matched healthy seniors (MNI coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI and VBM), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD per Rascovsky et al. criteria), I6 (between-group contrast bvFTD vs controls reported in MNI space), I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level VBM results reported), and I8 (coordinates/tables reported). I5 (minimum sample sizes): the document reports participants n=25 for the morphometry analysis with patients and healthy participants and reports a between-group voxelwise comparison, which reasonably indicates group sizes meet the >=6 requirement; therefore I5 is considered satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Reported peaks and thresholding are provided, and inference was whole-brain voxelwise. Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), has sufficient patient and control sample sizes (I5), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from the target bvFTD sample (I7), and reports coordinates/peaks (I8). However, the NeuroStore record shows only a within-group voxelwise regression (cross-subject association in the bvFTD patient group) and does not report any between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls in MNI/Talairach space. Inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5-E9) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded.

The paper reports whole-brain FDG-PET between-group contrasts for FTD and SD vs controls (Talairach coordinates), but it does not specify that the patient group is behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Control group sample size is not reported in the document, so the requirement for confirmed >=6 controls cannot be verified. Therefore the study does not meet the review’s required sample diagnostic definition (I4) nor the requirement to verify control group size (I5), and it does not provide a between-group contrast explicitly comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise result), I8 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria from the provided list were triggered.

The study uses VBM (structural morphometry) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (peaks/tables), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and sufficient sample sizes. However, it does not report a direct between-group VBM contrast comparing the bvFTD group against healthy controls (bvFTD not pooled with other patient groups) in stereotactic space. The listed analyses are cross-subject regression/correlations of structural measures with physiological responses across participants rather than explicit bvFTD vs. control group contrasts. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met; exclude.

The study is excluded because it does not provide a between-group contrast comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) group to controls. Instead, analyses are cross-subject regressions across a heterogeneous dementia sample (including Alzheimer’s disease, frontotemporal lobar degeneration/FTD, semantic dementia, posterior cortical atrophy), so results are not specific to a bvFTD group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging modality), I5 (sample size ≥6 participants overall/patient group), I8 (coordinates/whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not clearly present a distinct clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Picks disease group), I6 (no between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample). Exclusion criteria met: E7 (sample includes other forms of dementia/mixed diagnostic groups). Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for this review.

This study reports voxel-wise structural morphometry (VBM-like) analyses relating object memory to gray matter and lists whole-brain, MNI-coordinate results for a behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) sample compared with controls. The paper explicitly includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group, reports between-group (bvFTD vs control) voxelwise contrasts with reported peak coordinates (tables), and both patient and control groups exceed the 6-participant minimum (study abstract lists 13 bvFTD and 11 controls; NeuroStore analyses show group-level, whole-brain results). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for imaging modality, sample, sample size, between-group coordinate-based contrasts, and whole-brain reporting.

The study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (Lund and Manchester criteria) and healthy controls (21 bvFTD, 25 controls per abstract); resting-state fMRI and VBM were used. NeuroStore lists a between-group contrast Controls > bvFTD (analysis_3) using ICA dual regression, permutation voxelwise TFCE inference, with model fit and inference over whole brain and coordinate space MNI; reported peaks (Table t3) indicate whole-brain voxelwise results. Sample sizes exceed the ≥6 requirement. Thus it meets I3 (VBM/fMRI), I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (sufficient Ns), I6 (between-group MNI-space contrast for bvFTD vs controls), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level result), and I8 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record. No exclusions triggered.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients per consensus criteria (bvFTD) (I4). Patient group sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD n=16; controls n=18) (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls in standard space (MNI) with whole-brain inference (Controls > FTD; FWE voxel-level; reported coordinate peaks/tables) satisfying I6 and I7. Whole-brain results are clearly reported in tables (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is an empirical VBM study (not a review), reports whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and does not use excluded modalities only (DTI/FC/thickness). Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusions are triggered.

This study is excluded because it does not include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not met). The FTLD group is described as frontotemporal dementia/semantic dementia, with no indication of bvFTD-specific cases. Although the paper reports whole-brain voxelwise FDG-PET and MRI (VBM-like morphometry) results and adequate patient sample sizes, and coordinates are provided in tables, these meet I3, I5, and I8. The study does not report a between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met), nor does it clearly provide whole-brain group-level results identified as coming from a bvFTD sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study uses VBM (gray matter voxelwise morphometry) and includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) group with sufficient sample size (bvFTD n≈18) and healthy controls (n≈18). Whole-brain, voxelwise results are reported (tables of peak coordinates). However, the NeuroStore record only shows cross-subject voxelwise regression/correlation analyses (global performance, abstraction and linking ratios) across mixed groups (bvFTD, PSP, AD, controls) rather than a direct between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD versus controls where the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls unpooled) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I6. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Based on the requirement that ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study is excluded.

The study uses VBM (voxel-based morphometry) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample sizes; however, the reported neuroimaging results are cross-subject voxelwise regressions of self–informant discrepancy across a mixed sample (patients and controls) rather than a between-group, whole-brain VBM contrast that compares the bvFTD group directly to healthy controls without pooling with other patient groups. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I6 (no between-group BVFTD vs control contrast reported) and I7 (no whole-brain group-level result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group). Full text appears complete for screening.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (gray matter volume) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) (abstract: 10 bvFTD patients); has adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=10, controls n=10) (I5); reports a between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing Controls > bvFTD in MNI space (Analysis 23582296_analysis_0) where bvFTD is not pooled (I6); and explicitly reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (model fit over whole brain, voxel-wise GLM, reported peak coordinates/tables) (I7). The results are reported in tables of peaks (Tables tbl3/tbl4), satisfying I8. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met: this is an empirical VBM study with whole-brain results and no indication of excluded comorbid samples or ROI-only/DTI/FC-only methods. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the reported analysis used voxelwise model fitting but inference was restricted to a region of interest, so the paper does not present a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result for bvFTD (violates I7) and therefore meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only results). The study does meet I3 (VBM/structural morphometry), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample, n=26), and I6 (between-group contrast in MNI space comparing bvFTD to a disease control group). However, the control-group sample size is not reported in the document, so I5 cannot be confirmed. fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study used VBM (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=16) (I4). Sample sizes meet the minimum for patient and control groups (bvFTD n=16; controls n=34) (I5). However, the reported whole-brain analyses are cross-subject voxelwise regressions across the entire mixed sample (patients and controls) relating emotion-expression scores to gray matter; the paper does not report a between-group contrast comparing the bvFTD group to controls nor a group-level, whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text is complete enough for screening.

The study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and has sufficient patient sample size (n=56) (I5). However, it does not report any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups (I6 not met). Although one analysis is whole-brain, it reports an association across a mixed dementia patient cohort rather than a group-level, whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample; bvFTD-specific results are not reported whole-brain (I7 not met). Other analyses are restricted to ROIs. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this review and must be excluded.

The study meets imaging and sample inclusion criteria (I3 VBM; I4 clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample; I5 sufficient sample sizes; I6 reports between-group contrasts in MNI space comparing bvFTD to controls). However, all reported morphometric analyses were fit and inferred within a predefined CMS region-of-interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to ROI), and no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results are reported. This violates the requirement for at least one whole-brain (voxelwise) result (I7). Therefore the study is excluded under E6 (only ROI analyses, no whole-brain results).

Excluded because the patient sample is nonfluent variant primary progressive aphasia (nfvPPA), not behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4 not met). The reported analyses are within-group regressions in this nfvPPA subgroup and do not present a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met). Although the model was fit over the whole brain, statistical inference was restricted to a region-of-interest and reported results are ROI-limited, so no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample is provided (E6 applies; I7 not met). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (VBM structural morphometry) and I5 (patient group n=9 ≥6).

This VBM study includes bvFTD patients and uses whole-brain VBM (I3, I4, I5 met) but reports only within-patient analyses (presence of disgusting behaviors; cross-subject regression) in a heterogeneous neurodegeneration sample. No result is presented as a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups (I6 not met). Although analyses are whole-brain, they are not clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only sample (I7 not met). Coordinate space is listed as 'OTHER' rather than MNI/Talairach, further failing I6. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not report any between-group contrast comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls (Inclusion criterion I6 not met). It does meet multiple inclusion criteria: I3 (uses VBM/structural morphometry), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample per Neary criteria), I5 (n=91 patients, >6), I7 (reports at least one group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample — voxelwise multiple regression over whole brain with FWE correction), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/peaks). No exclusion criteria apply. Because the meta-analysis requires a between-group contrast (bvFTD vs controls) for inclusion, this within-group regression-only VBM study must be excluded.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), included a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (I4), had adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=18, controls n=27, overall n=67) exceeding the 6-participant minimum (I5), and reported at least one between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing bvFTD to controls in a standard stereotactic space (MNI) (I6,I7). Results are reported as peak coordinates/tables (I8). The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain VBM contrasts explicitly labeled “bvFTD > controls” (inference over whole brain, FWE-corrected), and multiple peak coordinates are provided. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not a review; not ROI-only; not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness; no evidence of disqualifying comorbid-sample issues). Therefore the study should be included for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

The paper uses VBM (gray-matter morphometry), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, and has adequate patient sample sizes (>6). However, all reported analyses are within-group cross-subject regressions across a mixed patient sample (multiple dementia diagnoses) and do not present a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing an isolated bvFTD group to controls. The record also does not show any whole-brain group-level voxelwise result explicitly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only sample. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6, E8, E9) are met based on the record.

The study uses voxelwise structural morphometry (gray matter VBM-like analysis) and includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (Neary criteria) with adequate sample sizes, so I3, I4, and I5 are satisfied. However, the reported group results do not provide an isolated, between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast of (behavioral) FTD versus controls: the between-group contrast pools controls with non‑overeating patients and contrasts against overeating patients, and the inference is restricted to an ROI despite a model fit over the whole brain. Analyses 1–2 are ROI-only. Thus the paper does not meet I6 or I7 (no clear bvFTD vs controls whole-brain voxelwise result) and it effectively reports only ROI-based inference, triggering exclusion criterion E6. Therefore the study is excluded.

Excluded because the paper does not provide a whole-brain, group-level VBM contrast comparing the bvFTD group to controls. Exclusion criterion met: E6 (only ROI analyses / no whole-brain results): although the VBM model was fit over the whole brain, inference was restricted to a region-of-interest, so no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise result is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients included). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (participant counts for the bvFTD group and controls are not provided/specified per group), I6 (no between-group VBM contrast reported that compares bvFTD to controls separately), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result identified as coming from the bvFTD sample). Full text appears complete in this extracted record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study uses FDG-PET (metabolic rate molecular imaging) in clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients and reports multiple between-group voxelwise contrasts (patients vs healthy controls) with coordinates in Talairach space. Whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference are explicitly reported for key contrasts. Patient and control group sizes exceed the minimum (several analyses report n=41–47 total), and results are reported as peaks/coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not using excluded modalities, and no indicated disallowed comorbidities). Therefore it satisfies the review inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8).

Excluded because the FTLD group combines multiple clinical subtypes (FTD, SD, PPA) without specifying behavioral-variant FTD or Pick's disease, so the sample does not clearly include bvFTD/Pick's disease (Inclusion I4 not met). The reported between-group contrast compares FTLD patients to early-onset AD patients rather than to healthy controls and does not present a between-group contrast of a bvFTD group versus controls (Inclusion I6 not met). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I5 (FTLD patient group n=14 ≥6), I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results), I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

The study uses VBM (gray matter volume), includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia with behavioral variant listed, and has sufficient patient sample size (n=72). However, the reported analysis describes overlap of atrophy between FTD and Alzheimer’s disease for IADLs (inclusive masking) and appears to be a cross-subject regression across patient groups; no healthy control group or a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls is reported. Although the model was fit voxelwise over the whole brain, the result is not clearly a group-level, whole-brain bvFTD-versus-control contrast. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I6 (between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls in stereotactic space) and I7 (clear whole-brain group-level result from the target bvFTD sample). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met.

The study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia group diagnosed by Neary/Lund & Manchester criteria, consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (I4). Patient group sizes meet the minimum (patients n=16; controls reported in abstract n=9) (I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing FTD to controls in MNI space (control > FTD) (I6) with whole-brain model fitting and voxel-level inference; peaks are reported in tables (I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical FDG-PET study with whole-brain results (E5,E6,E8,E9 not applicable). Minor uncertainty remains because the term “behavioral variant” is not verbatim in the record, but the clinical measures (NPI, behavioral deficits) and diagnostic criteria used strongly indicate bvFTD. Hence included with moderate-high confidence.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It uses VBM (I3) with gray-matter voxelwise analyses (FSL VBM). The sample includes clinically defined ALS-FTD patients meeting Neary criteria with prominent behavioral abnormalities reported (16 patients) consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (I4). Sample sizes satisfy minimums (88 patients; 15 neurologic disease controls) (I5). The abstract and reported analyses describe between-group, whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons implicating reduced GM in ALS-FTD versus controls in MNI space (voxel-level FDR thresholding) (I6,I7). Reporting of whole-brain results in tables/coordinates is present (reported peaks) (I8). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met based on the provided document. Minor ambiguity exists about explicit labeling as ‘bvFTD’, but Neary criteria plus behavioral abnormalities support inclusion as bvFTD. Full text is available in the provided record.

The study is excluded because it does not clearly specify that the patient sample comprises behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease (I4 not met). The record indicates clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia (FTD) assessed against FTLD criteria, but does not explicitly state bvFTD. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I5 (patient n=9 and control n=26 >=6), I6 (between-group contrast reported in stereotactic coordinates; 19 peaks reported), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported), I8 (results reported as coordinates/table). No exclusion criteria were met (none of E5–E9 apply based on the record). Full text was available in the record (fulltext_incomplete=false). Because I4 is not clearly satisfied, the study must be excluded for the bvFTD-focused review.

The study reports resting-state fMRI (ICA-based intrinsic connectivity) in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (Neary et al. criteria) and age-matched healthy controls (n=12 per group). It presents between-group cross-subject voxel-wise analyses (MNI space) and reports whole-brain inference with reported peak coordinates. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (>=6). Although some bvFTD patients had comorbid motor neuron disease, this does not conflict with the review inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (gray matter density) analyses (voxel-wise GLM) in patients with behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) and controls, with whole-brain inference and coordinates in MNI space. Sample sizes meet the minimum (bvFTD & controls: n=43; overall n=65). The paper presents between-group, whole-brain voxelwise results for bvFTD versus controls (reported peak coordinates/tables). Therefore it satisfies imaging modality (VBM), clinical sample (bvFTD), sample size, between-group MNI-space contrasts specific to bvFTD, and whole-brain group-level reporting.

Exclusion E9 applies: the study reports cortical thickness (structural morphometry) results only, which is explicitly excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (patient group n>=6 and control group present), I6 (between-group contrast bvFTD vs controls reported in MNI space), I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level result reported), I8 (results reported in tables of coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; it uses cortical thickness). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study uses VBM (gray matter volume) and includes 25 patients (meets I3 and I5). However, it reports only a within-patient cross-subject regression and does not present any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls (fails I6). Although the model was fit over the whole brain, inference was restricted to a region-of-interest so no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample is reported (fails I7). The sample appears to include mixed FTLD diagnoses (probable bvFTD or PPA), so I4 is not clearly satisfied. Therefore it meets exclusion E6 (only ROI analyses reported).

The study uses VBM and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses across an FTD patient sample (I3 and I5 met). However, it does not report a between-group contrast comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to healthy controls (I6 not met). The sample is mixed FTD cases (including semantic dementia and behavioural features) and is not clearly reported as a bvFTD-only group, so the target-sample requirement for bvFTD is not clearly satisfied (I4 not met). Although a whole-brain voxelwise regression is reported, it is not clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target group for the purposes of this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded because key inclusion criteria (I4, I6, I7) are not fulfilled.

This FDG-PET study reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (CTL > FTD) in MNI space and provides coordinate peaks. Modality is FDG-PET (I3). Participants are clinically diagnosed FTD patients using Lund and Manchester criteria (consistent with behavioral-variant FTD diagnosis in older literature) and include 29 patients and matched controls (meets I4 and I5). At least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result is reported and clearly identified as comparing the patient group to controls (I6, I7), and coordinates/results are reported in tables (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for bvFTD-related imaging evidence and is included.

The study uses FDG-PET (I3 satisfied) and has adequate sample sizes (patients n=29; overall n=45) meeting I5; results are reported in coordinate space and peaks are provided (I8 satisfied). However the paper reports ‘frontotemporal dementia’ without explicitly specifying behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease, so it does not meet I4 (must include clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease). Because I4 is not satisfied, the required between-group/bvFTD-specific criteria I6 and the bvFTD-targeted whole-brain requirement I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply based on the provided document. Therefore the study must be excluded from the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

The paper includes VBM-style structural morphometry (gray matter volume) and reports data from patients including bvFTD, with a large patient sample (n=75), so I3, I4 and I5 are satisfied. However, the reported whole-brain analysis is a cross-subject regression across a heterogeneous patient cohort (probability of laughing relative to partner's laughter) and does not present a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls that is not pooled with other patient groups. Thus it fails I6 (no bvFTD vs control between-group contrast in stereotactic space) and I7 (no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not provide the required bvFTD-specific between-group, whole-brain voxelwise result in MNI/Talairach space.

This task-based fMRI study explicitly examines behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) patients (n=15) versus healthy controls (n=11) using whole-brain voxelwise analysis in MNI space. Imaging modality is task fMRI (I3). The sample is clinically described as bvFTD (I4) with sufficient group sizes (I5). Multiple between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls are reported in MNI coordinates (I6). Critically, Analysis 25773639_analysis_0 reports a whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrast (controls > bvFTD) with FWE-corrected peak-level inference (I7). Results are reported in tables of peaks (Table tbl1), satisfying acceptable reporting (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (no review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no prohibited modality).

Imaging modality and sample: the study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) measuring gray matter volume (I3 satisfied). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4 satisfied) and group sizes meet minimums (bvFTD n=15; controls n=12) (I5 satisfied). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise morphometric analyses with coordinate tables (I8 satisfied). However, the reported between-group contrasts compare healthy controls to diagnostically heterogeneous patient subgroups defined by behavioral deficits (e.g., "temporal organization deficit group", "evaluation deficit group") rather than reporting a between-group whole-brain contrast of the bvFTD group specifically versus controls. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (bvFTD-specific between-group contrast) and I7 (whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD group) are NOT met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered based on the provided document.

This study is excluded because it does not report a clear between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD patients directly to healthy controls with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space (inclusion criterion I6 not met). The NeuroStore record shows whole-brain, voxelwise within-group DTI associations for the bvFTD group (analysis 3) and within- and between-patient-group regression analyses, and the abstract states VBM was used; thus inclusion criteria I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD sample present), I5 (patient and control group sizes >=6), I7 (at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target bvFTD group), and I8 (results reported in tables of peaks) are satisfied. However, no coordinate-based between-group bvFTD vs control contrast is reported in the extracted analyses or tables. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were met. Therefore the paper must be excluded for failing I6.

The study uses VBM and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (16 bvFTD) and meets minimum patient sample size, but it does NOT report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls. NeuroStore shows only within-group cross-subject VBM regressions across the combined FTLD cohort (n=26) and ROI-restricted contrasts; no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group versus controls is reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria from the review are triggered.

Study uses VBM (I3 met), includes sufficient sample sizes (16 patients, 9 controls; I5 met), and reports whole-brain voxelwise coordinates in tables (I8 met). However, the patient sample is described as mixed frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) including semantic dementia rather than specifically clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 NOT met). The paper does not report a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to controls; the between-group contrast is FTLD vs controls and key reported analyses are within-FTLD associations of eating behaviours (I6 NOT met). Because the results are not clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample, the requirement for a whole-brain group-level result from the target sample (bvFTD) is not satisfied (I7 NOT met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded.

The study used VBM (gray matter density) and includes clinically labelled behavioral-variant FTD cases with adequate patient counts, but the reported between-group contrast compares GRN- vs GRN+ patient subgroups rather than a bvFTD group versus healthy controls. No whole-brain group-level result is reported that clearly compares bvFTD patients to controls. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (no between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls in stereotactic space) and I7 (no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD-vs-control comparison).

The study uses VBM and reports whole-brain voxelwise morphometry and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, with sufficient patient counts and coordinate peaks reported (inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I7, I8). However, the NeuroStore extraction shows the reported between-group contrasts are bvFTD > AD and SD > AD and an AD within-group regression; no between-group, whole-brain contrast comparing bvFTD to healthy controls (in MNI/Talairach space) is reported. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (bvFTD vs controls contrast) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply based on the provided record. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I6 is not satisfied.

Excluded because the study does not provide a between-group, whole-brain VBM contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (I6 not met). While it uses VBM (I3) and has sufficient patient sample size for imaging analyses (n=17; I5 met), the participant sample comprises mixed FTD phenotypes (social/executive disorder, PNFA, semantic dementia, CBD, FTD-MND) and does not explicitly report results for a clinically diagnosed bvFTD/bvFTD-only group (I4 not clearly met). The reported voxelwise analyses are within-patient regressions (tau–atrophy) and subgroup comparisons within patients, not a bvFTD versus control whole-brain between-group contrast (I6 and I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Therefore the paper is not eligible for inclusion for a meta-analysis specifically targeting bvFTD group-level between-group voxelwise results.

The study uses VBM and includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients including bvFTD (I3, I4). Sample sizes appear adequate (n totals and subgroup sizes >6) and results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise coordinates/tables (I5, I8). HOWEVER, the paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain between-group contrast that is clearly specific to a bvFTD-only group compared directly to controls (contrasts report mixed FTD samples and subgroups defined by task performance, not a bvFTD vs control contrast). Therefore it fails I6 and fails I7 in the sense that whole-brain results are not clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Conclusion: EXCLUDE because I6 and I7 are not satisfied.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion requirements for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I5 (patient n=96, control n=34, both >6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 — the sample is described as ‘frontotemporal dementia (FTD)’ and references multiple diagnostic criteria (Rascovsky; Gorno-Tempini), but the document does not clearly indicate that clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) patients are identified as a distinct target group; I6 — no between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls is reported (analyses are within-group cross-subject regressions and ROI follow-ups); I7 — although whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported, they are not clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target group or reported as a bvFTD vs control group-level whole-brain contrast. No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly met. Full-text appears complete for screening.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for this review. Although it uses eligible imaging modalities (FDG-PET and structural morphometry consistent with VBM) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise within-group correlations in the FTLD subgroup with adequate patient sample size (n=9), the record does not explicitly state that the patient sample is behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease (I4 not met). Additionally, the extracted analyses are within-group correlations and the NeuroStore record does not provide any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD (or FTLD-subtype) group to controls in stereotactic space (I6 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text was available in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The paper studies frontotemporal dementia (FTD) but does not specify that the patient sample includes clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Picks disease. Analyses report FTD and primary progressive aphasia (PPA) together, so the target diagnostic group (bvFTD) is not clearly identified. While the study meets several methodological criteria (VBM whole-brain analysis, sufficient patient N, whole-brain voxelwise results reported in tables/figures), it fails to meet inclusion criterion I4 (bvFTD/Picks disease sample). It also fails I6 because the between-group contrasts compare an FTD group (not explicitly bvFTD) to controls. Therefore, it must be excluded.

The study reports voxel-based gray-matter morphometry analyses (VBM), so I3 is satisfied. However the document does not explicitly indicate inclusion of behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease specifically (I4 not met). The record gives only total N=36 without group counts, so I5 (>=6 patients per group and >=6 controls) cannot be confirmed. The reported analyses are voxelwise covariate regressions across patients and controls (associations with melody scores) rather than between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to controls, so I6 is not met. Although whole-brain voxelwise results are reported, they are not clearly reported as group-level results coming from a bvFTD group, so I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet key inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7).

Excluded because the reported analyses are region-of-interest only (Model fit over: region of interest) and no whole-brain voxelwise group results are reported (meets exclusion E6). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI used) and I5 (patient group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (paper does not explicitly state behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease; only ‘frontotemporal dementia’ is reported), I6 (no between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to healthy controls; reported contrasts compare FTD to AD), I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears available in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is excluded because it does not provide data from clinically defined bvFTD (or Pick’s disease) compared with healthy controls; instead it reports within-patient subgroup contrasts (patients with vs without urinary incontinence). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET metabolic imaging) and I5 (patient group sizes n=26 and n=44 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (sample not clearly identified as bvFTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls; contrasts are UIC vs non-UIC patient groups), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results are reported but not clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample required by the review objective). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Outcome: excluded due to failure to meet key sample/contrast criteria for a bvFTD vs control whole-brain comparison.

This study is excluded because it does not report the required between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) group to controls (inclusion criterion I6 not met). It does use VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within a mixed FTLD sample (I4), has >=6 patients (n=37) (I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (I7) with acceptable reporting (I8). However, the reported between-group contrasts compare musicophilic vs non-musicophilic patients within an FTLD cohort rather than bvFTD vs controls, and bvFTD is not isolated in a contrast against controls. Therefore it cannot be included in this meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not report results specifically from clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease groups, nor does it report any between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used) and I5 (patient group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no explicit clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease group reported), I6 (no between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls where bvFTD is not pooled), and I7 (no whole-brain group-level result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD/bvFTD-only sample). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered (e.g., ROI-only, review article). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

The study uses VBM and includes bvFTD cases but does not report a between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls. Included: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD cases included in the cohort), I5 (patient group sizes exceed 6 overall: FTLD n=58). Not met: I6 (no reported between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls; reported contrasts are symptomatic vs asymptomatic and C9orf72 subanalysis), I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only sample—the reported voxelwise inference is restricted to ROIs, and whole-brain uncorrected findings are reported for the FTLD cohort but not specifically for a bvFTD group). No exclusion criteria were triggered (e.g., this is not ROI-only reporting overall, not a review). Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

The study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (meets I4), and has adequate patient sample sizes (n=32) (meets I5). However, no healthy control group or any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls is reported; reported contrasts are between mutation subgroups (GRN+ vs GRN-) or regressions within patient/asymptomatic groups. Thus it fails I6 (no bvFTD vs control contrast) and does not provide a whole-brain group-level result clearly isolated to a bvFTD-only sample for inclusion (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded.

The study uses VBM (I3) and patient/control group sizes meet minimums (I5). However, the reported analyses use small-volume (ROI) FWE-corrected inference (inference restricted to region of interest) with no reported whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the target patient group; therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain results (I7) and effectively reports only ROI results (E6). Additionally, the patient group is reported as mixed frontotemporal dementia/semantic dementia (FTD and SD) and results are not presented as a direct bvFTD vs. control whole-brain contrast (I4 and I6 not met). Conclusion: Exclude for E6 (only ROI, no whole-brain results).

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused review. It uses FDG-PET and has an adequate patient sample (n=29) and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses; however the sample is described as frontotemporal dementia without explicit identification as behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) and all reported contrasts compare men vs women within the patient group rather than comparing a bvFTD patient group to healthy controls. Specifically, inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I5 (>=6 patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not explicitly state clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls in coordinate space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain result identified as a bvFTD vs control contrast). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete in the supplied record.

The study uses VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n>6), but the reported analyses are cross-subject within-group regressions with inference restricted to a region-of-interest (small-volume) rather than reporting any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls. Therefore it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group result from the target sample. It meets the ROI-only exclusion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM), I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (sample size ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI analyses reported).

The study reports FDG-PET (metabolic rate) voxelwise analyses (SPM96) in clinically characterized frontotemporal dementia patients (Lund and Manchester clinical criteria) and compares them with healthy subjects; sample size for the FTD group is 10 (>=6). The abstract and extraction indicate whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons with Talairach coordinates and reported peaks, and at least one between-group contrast involving the target FTD sample vs healthy controls is described in the abstract. Taken together this meets imaging modality (I3), target diagnosis (I4, Lund/Manchester criteria consistent with bvFTD classification), minimum sample size (I5), between-group contrast vs controls in stereotactic space (I6), whole-brain voxelwise result (I7), and acceptable reporting of coordinates/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria apply based on the document.

The study should be excluded because it reports only ROI-based voxelwise analyses (model fit and inference restricted to a mask of regions of atrophy), so it does not provide whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the target bvFTD sample. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET metabolic imaging), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; bvFTD n=24), I5 (patient sample n=38 >6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported comparing bvFTD to controls; analysis is a cross-subject regression within patient-related mask), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise result; inference restricted to ROI). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the paper does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and is excluded from the meta-analysis.

I excluded this study because the provided NeuroStore record does not clearly report a between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls (inclusion criterion I6 not met). The extraction also does not specify subgroup sample sizes for bvFTD or controls, so I cannot confirm the minimum of 6 participants per patient/control group (I5 not met). The study does meet I3 (uses VBM/structural morphometry), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD), and I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Because the record lacks explicit bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise coordinates/contrasts and subgroup counts, it cannot be included for the specified meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD (or Pick's disease) group to controls in MNI/Talairach space. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes Pick’s disease/autopsy-confirmed FTLD subgroups) and I5 (n=77, >6 patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls reported; analysis is a within-group cross-subject regression), I7 (no clearly identified whole-brain group-level result coming specifically from the target bvFTD/based subgroup), and I3 (imaging modality listed as “structural morphometry other” but not explicitly VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears accessible in the record.

Excluded because the paper does not report any between-group whole-brain contrasts that compare a bvFTD-only group to controls (I6 not met) and does not provide whole-brain results clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample (I7 not met). The study does meet several inclusion criteria: uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants in the sample (7 bvFTD cases) (I4), has >=6 patients in the bvFTD subgroup and control group sizes meet minimums (I5), and reports coordinate tables of whole-brain peaks (acceptable format) (I8). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the study is excluded from the review focused on bvFTD vs controls contrasts because the reported group-level voxelwise results pool bvFTD with other FTD phenotypes rather than providing bvFTD-specific between-group contrasts.

The study uses FDG-PET and includes an FTD patient subgroup (n=7), but it does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise results specifically comparing behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or clearly labeled FTD subgroup to controls. Extracted analyses only present contrasts for DLB and PD; no FTD/bvFTD contrast or whole-brain coordinate table for the target group is provided. Therefore key inclusion criteria requiring (I4) target diagnosis (bvFTD/Picks) specific results, (I6) a between-group MNI/Talairach contrast for the target group, and (I7) a whole-brain group-level result for the target sample are not met.

This study uses VBM (I3) and includes adequate patient and control sample sizes (I5). However it does not include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease group: patient subgroups are progressive non-fluent aphasia (PNFA), semantic dementia (SemD), and a ‘social/executive’ (SOC/EXEC) group that is not explicitly labeled or diagnosed as bvFTD (I4 not met). There is no between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met). Although whole-brain VBM results are reported, they are not clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample, so the whole-brain target-sample criteria are not met (I7, I8 not met). No exclusion criteria from the review are triggered.

The study used VBM (structural morphometry) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (bvFTD n=11) with an adequate control group (n=39), meeting I3, I4, and I5. However, the reported neuroimaging analysis is restricted to pre-specified anatomical ROIs ("Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest") and no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group to controls is reported. The available NeuroStore record indicates the reported analysis is a cross-subject regression across pooled patients (n=18) rather than a between-group voxelwise comparison of bvFTD versus controls. Therefore the study does not satisfy I6 (between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls unpooled) or I7 (whole-brain voxelwise result for target group) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text is sufficiently represented in the document, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (I4) with 11 bvFTD patients and 14 controls meeting the minimum sample size (I5), reports between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (Controls > bvFTD) in MNI space where the bvFTD group is not pooled (I6), and clearly provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I7) reported as peaks/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: it is an empirical VBM study with whole-brain results and not a review, ROI-only, or excluded modality. Some analyses also include other dementia groups, but dedicated bvFTD vs. control whole-brain contrasts are reported, satisfying target-sample requirements.

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) structural analyses (gray matter density) and includes a clearly defined behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) patient group (n≈10) and healthy controls. It provides at least one between-group, whole-brain, voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to controls (Analysis 24523434_analysis_1: control > Behavioural variant FTD) with results in MNI space and corrected voxelwise inference. Sample sizes meet the minimum (≥6). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. The extracted record is sufficient to identify whole-brain, group-level coordinates from the target bvFTD sample, so the study should be included in the meta-analysis of bvFTD imaging studies.

The study uses VBM (satisfies I3) but does not report a clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) group explicitly (only ‘frontotemporal dementia’ generically and lists primary progressive aphasia and Alzheimer’s disease in participant metadata), so I4 is not met. There is no clear between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space where the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I6 not met). Although 58 patients are reported, control group counts are not provided, so I5 (minimum group sizes for patient and control groups) cannot be confirmed. Whole-brain VBM results are reported but not identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample, so I7 is not met. No exclusion criteria from E5–E9 apply based on the provided record.

The study used VBM (I3 satisfied) and reports whole-brain voxelwise associations. However, it does not report results specific to clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not met), and no between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls is provided (I6 not met). The reported analyses are correlational associations across a heterogeneous pooled sample (patients with various dementias and controls), so there is no group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target group (I7 not met). Group sizes for any bvFTD subgroup are not specified, so the minimum patient-group sample size criterion cannot be confirmed (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper is excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not report a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) group to controls without pooling with other patient groups (Inclusion criterion I6 not met). Although the paper uses VBM (I3 satisfied), has adequate patient and control sample sizes (I5 satisfied), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (I7 satisfied), the sample is a heterogeneous mix of neurodegenerative diagnoses (FTD, SD, PNFA, AD, etc.) and the reported analyses are cross-subject regressions of interpersonal traits across the combined sample rather than a standalone bvFTD vs control group contrast. The record does not explicitly identify a bvFTD subgroup analyzed separately (I4 not clearly met). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply.

The study uses structural morphometry (gray matter volume, consistent with VBM) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within a large sample (n=187), so I3, I4 and I5 are met. However, the reported analysis is a cross-subject regression associating BIS score with gray matter across patients and healthy participants (an association in a pooled sample) rather than a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD patients to controls. No whole-brain group-level result is clearly identified as coming specifically from the bvFTD group. Therefore the study does not meet I6 (a bvFTD vs control between-group contrast in stereotactic space) nor I7 (a whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly from the target sample). No exclusion criteria apply. Excluded on the basis of failing inclusion criteria I6 and I7.

The study used VBM (gray matter volume) in a large clinical sample (n=123) diagnosed using Neary criteria for FTD and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for FTD subgroups. However, the paper does not report a between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing a behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group to healthy controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups. The diagnostic label is given as ‘frontotemporal dementia’/FTD but bvFTD-specific between-group contrasts versus controls are not presented in the extracted analyses. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (no bvFTD vs control whole-brain between-group contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM), I4 (clinical FTD sample per Neary criteria), I5 (≥6 patients), I7 (reports whole-brain group-level results identified as coming from the FTD subgroup). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text is complete in this record.

The study reports empirical whole-brain voxelwise neuroimaging results in clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD patients using both voxel-based morphometry (morphometric VBM results) and task-based fMRI (Moral Judgment Task). Patient and control group sizes exceed the minimum (patient and control groups ≥6). Multiple between-group contrasts (e.g., Control > bvFTD; interaction contrasts) are reported in MNI space with coordinate peaks and whole-brain inference, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-only FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only, and sample details exclude the listed comorbidities).

The study used VBM (satisfies I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM results across a mixed sample of dementia patients and controls. However, it does not report results specifically for a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) group nor a between-group whole-brain contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls. The VBM analysis is a cross-subject regression across pooled patient groups (Alzheimer’s, frontotemporal dementia, CBD/PSP) rather than a bvFTD vs control contrast. The report also does not provide clear group sizes for a bvFTD subgroup to verify I5. Therefore the paper does not meet required inclusion criteria I4, I6, and I7 (and I5 cannot be confirmed from the provided document). No exclusion criteria from the list are directly triggered by the provided record.

Excluded because E6 (study reports only region-of-interest analyses with no whole-brain results: 'Model fit over' and 'Inference restricted to' are ROI). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses structural morphometry/gray matter density consistent with VBM) and I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (number of bvFTD participants not reported, so minimum-6 requirement cannot be verified), I6 (no between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls reported; analyses are within-group regressions and intersections), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise results from the bvFTD group; analyses are ROI-restricted), I8 not satisfied because whole-brain results are not reported. Full text is complete for screening (derived NeuroStore record).

This VBM study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=21) and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM regressions in MNI space relating gray-matter volume to face-processing measures (satisfies I3, I4, I5, I7, I8). However, all reported analyses are within-group cross-subject regressions in the patient group; NeuroStore shows no between-group contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls in MNI/Talairach. Inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply.

Exclusion decision because the paper does not report a direct between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing the bvFTD group to controls unpooled (I6 not met) nor a group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample (I7 not met). Notes: (a) exclusion IDs met: none; (b) inclusion IDs met: I3 (VBM/structural morphometry used), I4 (bvFTD participants included; n=20), I5 (patient and control groups each >=6), I8 (whole-brain coordinates reported in a table/peaks in MNI); (c) inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no reported bvFTD vs control between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space), I7 (no whole-brain result explicitly identified as originating from the bvFTD group alone). The reported analyses are cross-subject regressions and shared-effects across diagnostic groups predicting sarcasm score, not a bvFTD-versus-control voxelwise group comparison, so the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria.

execution_stats.search_query: (behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia OR bvFTD OR frontal variant frontotemporal dementia OR frontotemporal dementia OR picks disease) AND (functional magnetic resonance imaging OR fMRI OR voxel-based morphometry OR VBM OR positron emission tomography OR PET)
